claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi alloy is a bulk, single-phase high-entropy alloy.
The starting CoCrFeNi alloy has a relatively coarse microstructure.
The starting CoCrFeNi alloy exhibits strongly temperature-dependent friction and wear.
A reactive surface coating or treatment will promote formation of a nanostructured lubricious tribolayer during sliding.
Reaction with the environment and frictional heat will form an amorphous or finely nanocrystalline oxide or intermetallic phase in situ.
The resulting adaptive nanocomposite tribofilm will refine dynamically under shear.
Ambient oxygen and frictional heat will produce a stable, lubricious surface layer from the reactive coating.
The in situ tribolayer will reduce interfacial shear strength.
The tribolayer will minimize direct metal-to-metal contact and thereby lower adhesive wear.
The adaptive layer will compensate for temperature-induced variations in deformation behavior.
Modified CoCrFeNi samples will maintain a relatively low and stable coefficient of friction from room temperature to 800 °C.
Modified CoCrFeNi samples will have significantly lower wear rates than unmodified CoCrFeNi across the entire room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi can show increased friction and wear at some temperatures because of inadequate surface protection and temperature-induced microstructural changes.
The intervention will be effective under dry or mildly oxidizing sliding conditions, typical industrial loads and speeds, and temperatures from 25 to 800 °C.
Highly corrosive environments or ultra-high vacuum may alter oxidation behavior enough to require re-evaluation of performance.
The optimal coating composition, thickness, and processing parameters remain undetermined.
Long-term tribolayer durability under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading remains uncertain.
Coated and uncoated CoCrFeNi controls will be tested under identical load, speed, atmosphere, and temperature steps while friction, wear, and tribolayer characteristics are measured.

The hypothesis is falsified if the coating fails to produce statistically significant reductions in both friction and wear across the full temperature range, or if the proposed stable adaptive tribolayer does not form.
